lesson_title: Kinetic Energy: Double the Speed, Four Times the Danger
hook_text: Double your speed and the crash gets FOUR times worse. One tiny ² in the formula decides it.
clip_script: A one-tonne car at 20 metres per second — 72 on the speedometer. Its kinetic energy: half of 1 000 times 20 squared — 200 000 joules. That is a 2 kilogram brick lifted to where the planes cruise, riding along on an ordinary trip. Now the driver doubles the speed to 40. Recount the wallet: 40 squared is 1 600 — 800 000 joules. Double the speed, FOUR times the energy, because the speed multiplies by itself. Four times the energy means four times the braking distance, and in a crash, four times the wreckage. A collision at 80 is four collisions at 40 happening at once. That little squared symbol is the whole science of speed limits.
visual_style: A car's energy shown as a stack of coins that suddenly quadruples when the speedometer doubles; braking distance bars stretch 1x to 4x; the ² glows red in the formula.
mood: Sober jolt delivered with clean arithmetic.
pacing: Calm setup at 72 km/h, sharp gear-change to the doubling, hammer-blow of the four-times reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and count a moving wallet yourself.
